source.title: Deep Limits and a Cut-Off Phenomenon for Neural Networks

record.file_problem: Text appears complete. The title varies slightly in the header, but the supplied paper is the identified study.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports experiments on how random initialization affects hidden-state mixing with depth, but does not measure gradient training or classification error as the claim versions require.
record.gate_note: The paper reports initialization-related mixing outcomes, including a cut-off in total variation distance to a point mass at zero. These results concern randomly initialized, untrained layer dynamics, not training outcomes; cited initialization and training findings are not this paper's results.
record.test_reason: The study measures untrained forward-propagation dynamics and proves limits for stationary layer compositions. It reports no optimization outcomes. Its activation-mixing results do not establish V4's learning speed or trainable depth, and the authors explicitly leave their relevance to training open.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors develop a geometric framework for deep-layer limits, demonstrate activation-mixing cut-offs under random initialization, and speculate that initialization variance could control initial nonlinearity. They leave the practical consequences for training unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments study randomly initialized layer dynamics and total variation mixing, rather than gradient-based training and classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported mixing behavior varies with activation function, width and initialization normalization; the alternative normalization delays the cut-off.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the tested finite-precision random initialization, TanH networks have reported mixing times of 9 layers at width 1 and 11 at width 2; width-1 SiLU has mixing time 7. The authors report cut-off behavior for these smooth activations, tentatively report no such cut-off for ReLU, and say alternative initialization scaling delays but preserves the cut-off.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Untrained random-layer networks can exhibit a sharp transition toward a point mass at zero with depth, depending on activation and initialization scaling.

record.problems: The experiments use a simple random-weight Markov-chain setup and finite precision 0.001. The principal curves are presented as figures without tabulated values; the text gives only qualitative cut-off descriptions and does not establish relevance to training.

untested.parts: Training classification error, CIFAR datasets, label corruption, model size, optimizers and training duration.
Teacher-student training, spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training degradation with depth and its prevention through identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Learning speed and trainable depth under activation-matched initialization; gradient preservation; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization; very deep convolutional training.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss recovery, curvature evolution, edge-of-stability training and divergence.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with batch normalization or Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The numerical mixing times are explicitly stated in figure captions. Row states here concern the supplied claim versions; they do not deny the reported mixing observations.

versions.untested_parts: Training error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, model size, optimizer and training duration.
Teacher-student optimization, spurious minima and student width relative to teacher width.
Training error across plain and residual networks, depth, shortcuts, normalization and special initialization.
Learning speed and trainable depth under different initializations; the experiments measure untrained activation mixing, not learning.
Training behavior across learning rates and sharpness or curvature.
Training speed, accuracy and learning-rate tolerance with and without batch normalization or Fixup.
